hook.text: Smoked salmon was originally a survival food—indigenous peoples smoked fish to last through harsh winters.

buildup.text: Wood smoke contains over 200 compounds including phenols, carbonyls, and organic acids. Each plays a preservation role.

discovery.text: Phenols are antioxidants that slow fat rancidity. Formaldehyde kills surface bacteria. Acids lower the pH.

twist.text: Modern 'smoked' foods often use liquid smoke—a concentrated extract. It adds flavor but provides much less preservation.

climax.text: Hot smoking (70–80°C) partially cooks food. Cold smoking (20–30°C) preserves without cooking—riskier but more complex in flavor.

punchline.text: Smoke dries, acidifies, and coats food with antimicrobial compounds. Triple defense.

quiz.question: What role do phenol compounds in smoke play in food preservation?
options: They act as antioxidants that slow fat rancidity
